correctness.rationale: Reconstructed F_n over F2 with kernel two constants for odd n or two parity classes for even n, and image exactly one or two parity constraints. The output rotation stabilizer has t=n/p elements; fixed-predecessor counts on each divisor repeat the linear inverse image on a length-pj ring. Burnside with totient sums gives every case including n=1,2. Independent implementation formed all rotation necklaces and inverse counts for EVERY input length 1..13 and matched all target degrees; the source checker separately specifies length<=16 (8923 target necklaces). Finite enumeration is corroboration only, not an all-length proof.
residual_risks: The case p even with nonzero primitive parity but t even requires Burnside on H, not just the existence of a labeled predecessor.
No dynamics of multi-step preimages, reversal quotient, or other binary rules has been proven.

value.rationale: Incoming degree on rotation-orbit state networks is a natural precise invariant for a foundational cellular automaton. The complete all-output classification of the symmetry-induced degree spectrum, with n=8 sharp realization and primitive-period boundaries, advances beyond the uniformly 2/4 labeled fibers and is useful for inverse-branching or quotient transition graphs. No downstream theorem is required.
residual_risks: If a hidden classical Ducci-square formula covers the result, its original-value basis would have to be revisited.

final_claim: For every n>=1 the immediate indegree of each output binary necklace under one cyclic Rule90 update is exactly determined by its primitive block parity and t=n/p; possible degrees 0,1,2,3,4, all realized by n=8.
limitations: Only binary synchronous one-step Rule90 modulo rotations; no reflections/complements.
Independent finite checker through n=13, source verifier design through n=16, unbounded theorem relies on proved Burnside argument.
